research_text:
## Research brief

### API and reported value

`java.security.MessageDigest` computes a fixed-length digest of supplied data. The algorithm is selected by the `algorithm` string passed to the static `getInstance` factory. Data is supplied through `update` and finalized through `digest`; `digest(byte[])` performs a final update itself. Finalization resets the object. Oracle API: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/java/security/MessageDigest.html ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/java/security/MessageDigest.html))

The reported message is consistent with a detector evaluating a factory’s algorithm argument as `SHA1` against an allow-list. It does **not**, by itself, establish the call target, runtime value, digest purpose, or complete event trace. The supplied message lists six spellings; the CrySL source’s algorithm constraint lists only the three hyphenated spellings. The source does not explain that discrepancy. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl))

### Documented usage and security guidance

The Java API accepts documented algorithm names and gives `SHA-256` as an example; it also documents `SHA-1`. Its API documentation does not prescribe a universal remediation for every SHA-1 use. NIST separately recommends that federal agencies transition away from SHA-1 and use SHA-2 or SHA-3 alternatives. NIST’s guidance is application-dependent, particularly for uses requiring collision resistance. NIST policy: https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/hash-functions/nist-policy-on-hash-functions ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/java/security/MessageDigest.html))

A digest equality comparison alone does not establish that the digest provides authentication or adversarial integrity. The sources and finding do not identify whether this digest is a cache key, runtime discriminator, persisted identifier, security digest, or part of an external contract.

### Compatibility and migration

- **Output and formats:** SHA-1 produces 160 bits; SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 produce 256, 384, and 512 bits respectively. Thus, changing algorithms changes the digest value and length; compatibility with persisted values or wire protocols depends on the applicable format or peer contract. Oracle algorithm names: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/specs/security/standard-names.html ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/specs/security/standard-names.html))
- **Platform support:** Java SE 8 requires support for SHA-1 and SHA-256, but its API documentation does not require SHA-384 or SHA-512. Java SE 26 requires SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-384; it does not list SHA-512 as mandatory. A particular provider’s support must also be considered. Java SE 8 API: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/MessageDigest.html ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/MessageDigest.html))
- **Migration path:** NIST notes that SHA-1 may still be necessary to handle information protected before its planned December 31, 2030 transition date. The Java API sources reviewed do not specify a general persisted-format or wire-format migration procedure. NIST announcement: https://csrc.nist.gov/news/2022/nist-transitioning-away-from-sha-1-for-all-apps ([csrc.nist.gov](https://csrc.nist.gov/news/2022/nist-transitioning-away-from-sha-1-for-all-apps?utm_source=openai))

### Exact CrySL matching clause

The referenced, mutable `master` source is: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl

Its relevant clauses are, verbatim: ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl))

```text
SPEC java.security.MessageDigest
```

```text
g1: getInstance(algorithm);
g2: getInstance(algorithm, _);
Get := g1 | g2;
```

```text
algorithm in {"SHA-256", "SHA-384", "SHA-512"};
```

The file declares `algorithm` as `java.lang.String`. The acquisition events name **`getInstance` on the specified `java.security.MessageDigest` type** and specify either one parameter or two, with the second represented by `_`. The condition tests membership of the first argument in the three quoted strings. `getInstance` is static, so it has no instance receiver. The rule file also declares `update` and `digest` events and separate sequence and bounds constraints. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl))

**A method merely sharing the name is not, on that basis alone, a declared event of this specification:** the file specifies `java.security.MessageDigest` and parameter-shaped events, not a name-only wildcard. The file itself does not document every detail of a particular scanner’s type resolution or matching implementation, so it cannot establish how that scanner handled the reported location. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl))

One correction to the supplied summary: the source defines the post-update alternative using `Digest`, which includes `digest(input)` as well as `digest()` and `digest(output, offset, len)`. It therefore also permits a modeled `update` followed by `digest(byte[])`. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/MessageDigest.crysl))

### Source limits

The reviewed rule is the current content of a mutable branch, not a verified copy of the rule revision bundled with the reporting detector. The supplied SHA-256 identifier was not independently verified. The finding lacks a resolved-call trace and runtime context, and the rule file does not explain the detector’s six-spelling message or its treatment of unresolved values.
